planting.note: Plant certified disease-free rhizome pieces with at least one visible eye once soil has warmed in spring.

directions: Chinese Yellow is the large-rhizome, mild-flavored ginger type most commonly sold fresh in American and Asian grocery markets, distinguished from Hawaiian Yellow and Bubba Blue strains by its paler, less fibrous flesh and lower pungency. Plant rhizome pieces 2-3 inches deep in loose, rich, well-drained soil after the soil has warmed in spring. Provide dappled shade during the hottest afternoon hours and consistent moisture through the long 8-10 month growing season; mature rhizomes are ready to dig once the foliage yellows and dies back in fall. In zone 9a, dig and store rhizomes indoors over winter or heavily mulch in a well-protected bed, since prolonged soil temperatures below the upper 40s Fahrenheit will rot the rhizome.
sources: University of Hawaii CTAHR Ginger Production Guide

planting.note: Plant finger rhizomes 2 inches deep once soil has warmed in spring.

directions: Lakadong is a high-curcumin turmeric selection originating from the Jaintia Hills of Meghalaya in northeast India, prized by growers and herbalists for curcumin content that runs well above ordinary supermarket turmeric. Plant finger rhizomes in rich, well-drained soil in partial shade once the soil has warmed in spring, and keep the bed evenly moist through the long frost-free growing season the crop needs to bulk up. Foliage dies back naturally in fall, signaling that rhizomes are ready to dig, cure, and either replant or process into powder; in zone 9a, lift and store rhizomes indoors over winter rather than relying on the ground to protect them. The deep-orange flesh and intense color make Lakadong a favorite for home turmeric powder as well as fresh-root use.

planting.note: Plant divisions with several canes attached once night temperatures stay reliably warm.

directions: Eileen McDonald is a soft pink-bracted selection of red ginger, sharing the same cane-like stems and glossy tropical foliage as the species but replacing the typical scarlet flower spike with a delicate blush-pink one. Plant divisions with several canes attached in rich, organic soil in a warm, humid, partially shaded site protected from wind, since the tall canes can be toppled in storms. Keep soil consistently moist and feed regularly through the growing season to encourage the long-lasting bracts, which are popular in cut tropical flower arrangements. This selection is hardy only in the warmest zone 9b-10 gardens and is best grown in a large container that can be moved under cover, or treated as a die-back perennial with heavy winter mulch in zone 9a.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions once soil has warmed and frost risk has passed.

directions: Orchid ginger forms handsome clumps of cane-like stems clothed in glossy, deep-green lance-shaped leaves, topped from spring through fall by upright spikes of small cream-to-pale-yellow flowers with an orchid-like lip. Plant rhizome divisions in humus-rich, well-drained soil in a warm, humid, partially shaded location sheltered from harsh afternoon sun and drying wind. Keep the root zone consistently moist during active growth and ease off watering somewhat in cooler months, since the plant slows but does not go fully dormant in mild climates. In zone 9a, grow it in a large container that can be sheltered over winter, or site it in a protected microclimate and mulch the crown heavily, since foliage is damaged by frost and the rhizome can be lost in a hard freeze.

planting.note: Plant rhizomes 2-3 inches deep after the danger of frost has passed.

directions: Chiang Mai Snow is a white-bracted selection of Siam tulip, sharing its Thai wild origins with the well-known pink 'Chiang Mai Pink' but replacing the rosy bracts with cool, papery white ones held above narrow, upright green leaves. Plant rhizomes 2-3 inches deep in rich, well-drained soil in dappled shade after frost danger has passed, and keep the bed evenly moist through the summer bloom period. Foliage and flower stalks die back naturally as the plant goes dormant in fall; lift rhizomes and store them dry and frost-free over winter in zone 9a, since the species is not reliably hardy outside the warmest coastal gardens. The tidy, compact habit and long-lasting cut flowers make this cultivar a popular container and border specimen.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions once soil is warm and frost risk has passed.

directions: Zingiber darcyi is a Thai species grown chiefly for its intensely fragrant flowers, which emerge low among the reed-like stems as white and burgundy-purple blooms with a sweet, carrying scent. Plant rhizome divisions in humus-rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in a warm, humid, partially shaded spot, since strong direct sun scorches the broad leaves. Keep the planting consistently watered through the growing season and mulch generously to conserve moisture around the shallow rhizomes. In zone 9a, treat this ginger as a container plant that can be moved to shelter for winter, or plant it in a favorable microclimate and mulch heavily, since it is less cold-hardy than common shampoo ginger and can be lost to a hard freeze.

planting.note: Plant rhizomes once soil has warmed and frost risk has passed.

directions: Bridal Bouquet ginger produces broad, richly veined tropical foliage and, on separate leafless stalks, striking cone-like flower spikes of pure white bracts that resemble a bouquet held just above the soil line. Plant rhizomes in rich, evenly moist, well-drained soil in filtered light or morning sun with afternoon shade, since intense sun scorches the large leaves. Water generously through the warm growing season and allow the foliage to die back naturally in fall as the plant enters winter dormancy. In zone 9a, lift and store rhizomes indoors over winter, or grow the plant in a container that can be moved to a warm, dry, frost-free space until the following spring.

planting.note: Plant rhizome divisions once soil has warmed and frost risk has passed.

directions: Bengal Tiger ginger is grown primarily for its bold, dark-green foliage marked with irregular chartreuse and cream stripes, forming an upright clump of reed-like stems and valued more for foliage than for its inconspicuous flowers. Plant rhizome divisions in rich, well-drained, evenly moist soil in partial shade, since the variegated leaves can bleach or scorch in strong direct sun. Feed and water generously through the growing season to keep the foliage lush, and expect the plant to die back to the rhizome with cooler fall temperatures. In zone 9a, dig and store rhizomes in a frost-free location over winter, or maintain the plant in a large container that can be sheltered indoors until spring.
